letters.desc: AEP argues that Commission reforms should be principles-based and avoid prescriptive one-size-fits-all requirements, preserving the ability of states and regions to tailor solutions to their specific large load growth needs.
quotes: Any rules adopted by the Commission in this proceeding should be principles-based, avoid prescriptive requirements, and allow for regional flexibility.
The Commission's reforms should avoid introducing additional delays to large load interconnection by disrupting state and regional-level efforts.

letters.desc: Chevron argues FERC should let ISO/RTOs adopt variations on national large load standards suited to regional circumstances, following the same model used in generator interconnection under Orders 2003, 845, and 2023. It contends this accelerates adoption without sacrificing the national baseline.
quotes: The Commission should take a similar approach with respect to large load interconnections.

Allowing for appropriate flexibility should facilitate the adoption of large load interconnection standards by ensuring that such standards can be efficiently and expediently implemented according to each region's needs.
The Commission should act quickly, while avoiding distracting jurisdictional disputes with states and accommodating constructive regional proposals.

letters.desc: EEI supports allowing RTOs and regions to set or adjust the MW threshold above the federal floor to account for local system conditions, avoiding a one-size-fits-all national rule.
quotes: any nominal threshold should be subject to adjustment to reflect regional and local concerns.

letters.desc: LPPC urges FERC to defer to existing regional protocols on size thresholds and study processes, noting that prescriptive national rules could undermine regions that already have functioning large load interconnection procedures.
quotes: LPPC asks the Commission to defer to varied regional approaches. Utilities across the country and ISOs/RTOs have set varied thresholds for the definition of large loads, based on judgments regarding grid configuration and available transmission capacity. LPPC is of the view that the 20 MW threshold is low, and that loads substantially larger than 20 MW have been integrated with some frequency under state-based protocols.

letters.desc: The filer requests that the Commission refrain from imposing uniform national rules and instead encourage section 205 filings and region-specific solutions that reflect MISO's unique composition of obligation-to-serve utilities and state-led resource adequacy.
quotes: the MISO Transmission Owners welcome any and all support from the Commission that avoids a "one-size-fits-all" approach and provides flexibility and encourages Federal Power Act section 205 filings to craft innovative solutions that optimize regional differences in achieving timely, reliable, and affordable speed to power.

letters.desc: National Grid supports a final rule that sets a federal baseline while allowing ISOs, RTOs, and transmission owners to adapt requirements to regional market characteristics. Regions with existing procedures should be allowed to build on them rather than start over.
quotes: The NYISO already has procedures in place to study large loads interconnecting to the transmission system.  Allowing the NYISO and other regions to leverage these existing processes will help avoid unnecessary delays and support innovation.

letters.desc: ODEC supports a Final Rule that sets binding national standards while allowing transmission providers to demonstrate compliance through regionally tailored approaches, provided those approaches meet or exceed the rule's requirements.
quotes: the Commission should use this proceeding to provide clarity and a set of policies or principles that must be adopted by transmission providers, with flexibility for regional differences.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The SPP TO Group argues that any final rule must include an explicit independent entity variation standard so that RTOs and ISOs, especially SPP, can maintain region-specific programs already under development. The group notes that SPP and MISO differ structurally from PJM in utility ownership and transmission topology, making one-size rules unworkable. Delaying or overriding SPP's pending HILL proposals would be a serious error.
quotes: it would be a serious error to force the region to pause this work to await a nationwide rule.

any nationwide rule addressing interconnection practices should expressly permit regional flexibility, particularly for regions like SPP that have already been working diligently to advance policies consistent with those of the Commission and DOE.

the characteristics of regions such as SPP and MISO that are largely composed of vertically-integrated and investor-owned utilities are materially different than other regions, such as PJM, that include numerous states with retail open access policies as well as several wires-only transmission and distribution utilities.

letters.desc: IECA opposes imposing a mandatory federal interconnection process nationwide, arguing the Southeast and parts of the West are succeeding without delays and that a blanket rule would produce unintended consequences and slow successful markets.
quotes: we also urge the Commission to recognize regional differences and not impose a new mandatory interconnection process on those regions experiencing rapid load growth from large loads, which are not experiencing interconnection challenges or delays.

Conversely, we also recognize that in the Southeast and some areas in the West a significant amount of Data Center load growth is occurring without the same large load interconnection delays facing other areas. In those States, there is no compelling reason to alter the already successful large load interconnection processes for Data Centers in those States.

we suggest that any load interconnection program that the Commission may introduce should not be mandatory across the entirety of the U.S., i.e., a one-size-fits-all approach is not the best way forward.
